questions.stem: A vulnerability scan differs from a penetration test in that it:

choices.A: Actively exploits vulnerabilities to confirm severity
choices.B: Automatically identifies known vulnerabilities and misconfigurations without exploitation

questions.explanation: Vulnerability scanning uses automated tools to probe for known vulnerabilities and misconfigurations. Penetration testing goes further by actually exploiting findings.

questions.stem: A CVSS score of 9.8 is classified as:
questions.explanation: CVSS: 0.0=None, 0.1-3.9=Low, 4.0-6.9=Medium, 7.0-8.9=High, 9.0-10.0=Critical. A score of 9.8 is Critical and requires urgent remediation.

questions.stem: Patches should be tested in staging first to:

choices.A: Verify patches don't cause instability or application breakage before production deployment
choices.B: Give attackers time to analyse the patch
choices.D: Allow the vendor to recall defective patches

questions.explanation: Testing in a production-mirror environment finds compatibility issues before patches affect critical business systems.

choices.A: A new OS version has different default settings
choices.B: Patch management tools fail to update automatically
choices.C: Systems gradually deviate from the approved security baseline due to unmanaged changes
choices.D: An organisation adopts a new security framework

questions.explanation: Configuration drift is the gradual divergence of system configuration from its approved baseline, caused by manual changes, updates, or user modifications.

questions.stem: A 90-day delay on a CRITICAL CVE where the SLA is 30 days represents:

choices.B: A governance failure showing the patch process is not functioning as designed
choices.C: Acceptable exception if no active exploitation is observed
choices.D: A configuration management issue unrelated to patching

questions.explanation: Exceeding the defined SLA for a CRITICAL vulnerability with an available patch demonstrates the patch process is broken, creating documented organisational negligence.

choices.B: Unauthorised changes to monitored system files, directories, or configuration settings

questions.explanation: FIM continuously compares the current state of files and configurations against an approved baseline, alerting on unauthorised modifications including those made by malware.

questions.stem: A compensating control for a system that cannot be immediately patched is:

choices.A: Ignoring the vulnerability until the next maintenance window
choices.C: Network segmentation, IPS signatures for the CVE, and enhanced monitoring while expediting the patch process

questions.explanation: Compensating controls reduce risk when the preferred control cannot be immediately applied. Segmentation limits exposure; IPS virtual patching blocks known exploit traffic.

questions.stem: Formal change management requires before any system modification:

choices.B: Documentation of what changes, who approved it, and the rollback procedure

questions.explanation: Formal change requests document the change, justification, security impact, approvals, and rollback procedures, ensuring changes are deliberate and reversible.

choices.A: IPS signatures or WAF rules that block exploitation of a known vulnerability without modifying the vulnerable application
choices.B: Applying the vendor patch ahead of the testing schedule
choices.C: Running the vulnerable application in a sandboxed container
choices.D: Rolling back to a previous version

questions.explanation: Virtual patching uses IPS/WAF rules to block known exploit traffic, providing interim protection while the formal patch is tested and deployed.

questions.stem: A security baseline configuration document defines:

choices.A: All software vulnerabilities found in a system
choices.B: The incident response procedure for that system
choices.C: The approved security settings all systems of that type must match at deployment and maintain over time
choices.D: The backup schedule and retention period

questions.explanation: A security baseline documents the approved configuration state. Deviations require formal change management approval and trigger configuration drift alerts.
